## Summary
- Rename the internal handoff policy helper to `computeDeterministicTransition` and add planner-facing deterministic suggestion generation.
- Emit `ORCHESTRATOR_SUGGESTED_*` fields from orchestrator preflight into the planner prompt while keeping runtime validation mandatory.
- Preserve delegated child issue execution as the deterministic worker chain and update docs/workflow descriptions to treat `heuristics` as a compatibility alias.

## Tests
- `npm run build`
- `node --test dist/__tests__/handoff.test.js`
- `node --test dist/__tests__/orchestrator-preflight-cli.test.js`
- `node --test dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`
- `node --test dist/__tests__/orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.js`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #367

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #377 implements phase 1 of #367: it reframes the old `heuristics` concept as deterministic transition policy rather than a primary public orchestrator mode. It renames the transition helper, adds planner-facing deterministic suggestion outputs, threads those outputs through orchestrator preflight into the planner prompt, and keeps runtime validation mandatory. It also preserves delegated child issues as deterministic worker chains and updates docs/workflow descriptions so `heuristics` is treated as compatibility behavior. The broader goal is to make agent-mode orchestration the public default while retaining deterministic policy as a safety and execution guardrail.

## Review
The implementation matches the approved phase-1 plan and the core wiring looks sound. The only unresolved actionable concern is prompt-level: the new deterministic suggestion wording gives the planner a default path, but it still does not encode the selected one-shot follow-up guardrail for later user-launched follow-up rounds.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| One-shot follow-up guardrail missing from planner prompt | WARNING | The prompt tells the planner to use the deterministic suggestion as the default, but it does not remind agent-mode planning to stop on second-or-later user-launched follow-up rounds unless the user explicitly requested continued automation. |

## Progress
- No existing inline review comments or review threads were present, and no new inline comment was posted because the rubrics review already covers this same prompt concern in the PR discussion.
- Reviewer disagreement: Codex found no blocking or warning issues; Claude raised low-risk hardening notes; the rubrics reviewer flagged the one-shot prompt gap as a warning.
- Claude’s type-hardening notes around `transitionToSuggestion()` are optional: the current deterministic transition table always sets `nextAction` for dispatch decisions, so they are not treated as required branch changes.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>One-shot follow-up guardrail missing from planner prompt</summary>

**Cause:** The new deterministic suggestion section in [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/90a0fb400fcb861da029a4b8e8ef3fad78be0e59/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L30-L35) says to use the suggestion as the default path, but it does not include the selected rubric’s constraint that second-or-later user-launched follow-up rounds should default to stopping unless continued automation was requested.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a concise prompt rule, likely under Runtime Policy or Instructions, telling the planner to default to `stop` for later user-launched follow-up runs unless the request asks for automation, full pipeline, auto-fix, or continued handoff. Keep normal orchestrator-launched chains and deterministic worker-chain behavior unchanged.

**Comments:** This is a prompt-policy gap rather than a runtime validation bug. It is concrete and safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: the unresolved warning is a concrete prompt change and is safe for automated branch repair.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items
- [ ] Add one-shot follow-up guidance to the orchestrator planner prompt so second-or-later user-launched follow-up rounds default to stopping unless continued automation is explicitly requested.

Yes, for the **public/user-facing surface**, that variable should go away.

The reason is that after this change, `AGENT_AUTOMATION_MODE` is no longer a meaningful user choice. Describing:

```yaml
automation_mode:
  description: "Post-action orchestration mode (agent public default; heuristics is a compatibility alias)"
```

still teaches users that there are modes they should think about. That is exactly the wrong tone and product surface. `heuristics` should be an internal compatibility/execution detail, not a documented option.

I would handle it as:

- Remove `AGENT_AUTOMATION_MODE` from public docs/config docs.
- Stop wiring public entry workflows through `${{ vars.AGENT_AUTOMATION_MODE || 'agent' }}`; just use `agent`.
- Remove or hide `automation_mode` from user-facing `workflow_dispatch` inputs where possible.
- Keep lower-level internal compatibility only where runtime still needs it, especially for existing installed repos and delegated child worker-chain behavior.
- Rename/refactor the remaining internal use later so it no longer looks like a public “mode” selector.

So: **yes for docs and public workflow surfaces; not necessarily a blind delete from every internal file in the same PR unless we also replace the internal compatibility path.**
